minutes.headline: ZBA voted to grant a special permit for a new house at 49 Brookview Terrace, waiving lot and one-year occupancy rules.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard a single application from Damon McQuaid to build a new residence on an undersized lot and convert the existing house to an accessory dwelling unit. Neighbors supported it by letter and in person, and no one opposed. The board moved, seconded and voted to grant the permit as requested, then adjourned.

public_comment.topic: A neighbor living directly across the street spoke in support, relaying his wife's view as an architectural conservator that the home would be an asset to the community.

votes.motion: Grant the special permit as requested: relief for lot area, lot width through the building, and the one-year accessory dwelling waiting period.

decisions.decision: Board agreed to waive the one-year waiting period to occupy the accessory dwelling, as requested.
Applicant and board concluded no height relief is needed, as the bylaw exempts non-habitable features such as the tower.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted to grant the special permit for a new house at 49 Brookview Terrace, with relief for lot area and lot width.
The board agreed to waive the one-year waiting period before the accessory dwelling can be occupied, as the applicant requested.
The application would build a new residence on an undersized lot and convert the existing house to an accessory dwelling unit.
The applicant and board concluded no height relief is needed, because the bylaw exempts non-habitable features such as the tower.
A neighbor across the street spoke in support; no opposition was recorded.

why_it_matters: A lot below the minimum size can still get a house through a special permit, and the same permit can waive the one-year wait to occupy an accessory dwelling, so a neighbor's lot may be developed differently than the zoning table suggests.
